Partly. The June 2025 finding still holds for the period it covered, 2021–2024, but it no longer covers the property's current status. It was superseded by a newer assessment (version 2, knowledge date 2026-11-12) that extends through 2025.

The new version flags a tree-cover loss candidate of 13.5 ha (3.9% of the asset) in 2025, on a property of 345.6 ha. The JRC 2020 forest reference agrees on 98% of the event area. The status is "pending corroboration" because 2025 is the latest year in the series, and a later year is needed to confirm persistence.

The evidence does not establish whether this was deforestation, since it could be harvest or other stand replacement. It also says nothing about cause, legality or compliance.

I'd update the file to note the 2025 candidate event and recheck once the next year of data is available.
